chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a slave girl shared between two men who had both manumitted her partially, then one of them made her private part permissible to his partner. He said: "It is permissible for him, and whichever of them dies before his partner, half of her becomes free from the side of the one who died, and the other half remains manumitted."

I said: What do you think if the remaining one of them wants to have intercourse with her? He said: "No, unless he establishes her manumission and marries her with her consent, a marriage with a dowry whenever he wishes."
I said to him: Hasn't half of her become free? She has owned half of her neck, and the other half belongs to the remaining one who manumitted her? He said: "Yes."
I said: If she makes her master permissible in her marriage and makes that permissible for him, he said: "That is not permissible for him."

I said: Why is it not permissible for him, just as you permitted the one who owned half of her if he made her private part permissible to his partner? He said: "Indeed, the free woman does not give away her private part, nor lend it, nor make it permissible, but she has a day from herself and the one who manumitted her has a day. So if he wishes to marry her for enjoyment in the day in which she owns herself, he may enjoy from her, whether little or much."

And whenever this manumitted slave girl gives birth, her child will be slavery for her master, unless the one who made it permissible for him had stipulated freedom for him, for then he becomes free by the previous condition, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَحَلَّ فَرْجَهَا: Made her private part permissible (for sexual relations)
key_terms.دَبَّرَهَا: Manumitted partially (specifically, declared free upon death or in stages)
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: For enjoyment (temporary marriage or specific right of use)
key_terms.نِصْفُ رَقَبَتِهَا: Half of her neck (referring to partial manumission status)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave girl shared by two masters when one dies or wishes to marry her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the complex fiqh of partial manumission (*kitaabah*) for a slave girl shared by two masters, establishing that upon one master's death, his share of her freedom is immediately realized. It further clarifies the distinction between a partially free woman's right to her own person versus the master's right to her body, noting that while she cannot simply 'gift' her chastity to the surviving master, he may marry her with her consent and a dowry. The ruling also addresses the status of offspring, determining whether they remain in bondage or gain freedom based on the specific conditions set by the master who granted the release.
